response.query: What exact static→dynamic calibration protocol (sample size per label, sampling stratification, acceptance thresholds for precision/recall) will validate static detector signals against build and runtime outcomes?
response.answer: Use dynamic thresholds for calibration, with stratified sampling and precision/recall thresholds set at 90% minimum. Validate against build and runtime outcomes with a sample size of at least 100 stratified labels.

results.title: Detector Best Practices: Static Thresholds - Splunk Community
results.content: If a signal goes above or below a static threshold or is within or outside a specified range, an alert will fire. This detector alerts on a synthetic test when uptime drops below the 90% static threshold:. While configuring static thresholds on SLOs is possible, within Splunk Observability Cloud it’s recommended to manage SLO alerts using error budgets. If you’re just starting out on your observability journey, using static thresholds is also a great way to capture baseline metrics and gain insight into trends so you can fine-tune and adjust your detectors and alerts. As we saw in the CPU detector above, alerting on static thresholds can lead to a lot of alert noise if not used correctly. **Note**: monitoring the CPU static threshold *combined* with pod queue length could provide the additional context needed to create an actionable detector. Applications with such variable traffic fluctuations might not benefit from alerting on static thresholds alone. For predictable, critical metrics static thresholds are a great alerting option.

results.title: What is static and dynamic image analysis?
results.content: Home > Learn > Bettersize Wiki > What is static and dynamic image analysis? # What is static and dynamic image analysis? **Static and dynamic image analysis** is a method utilized to determine particle size distribution and particle shape parameters according to their particle projections onto the acquired picture processed by the analysis software. **The difference between static and dynamic image analyses is the relative motion between the sample and the lens of the camera.**. In **static image analysis**, the sample is statically located on the carrier, above which a camera is installed for image capturing. For **dynamic image analysis**, particles pass through the focal plane of the camera to be captured clearly. For both image analyses, cameras with different magnifications are available for image acquisition of particles with different particle size ranges. How are particles dispersed when using the wet method? In laser diffraction particle size analysis, inaccurate results can be caused by particles agglomerating in the suspension, especially when they are fine. Therefore, a full dispersion of the sample prior to measurement is essential. How are particles dispersed when using the dry method? Samples that either dissolve or agglomerate in a wet medium or react with the medium are usually analyzed using the dry dispersion method. Obscuration refers to the proportion of light scattered and absorbed by the particles in the measurement zone, which indicates the concentration of the suspension. What is the background signal? A background measurement has to be made prior to sample analysis. The background measurement is made up of both optical and electrical signals. The absorption coefficient is a measure of the light beam penetration through a material. What are the factors that affect background? The reasons for abnormal background signals vary. The exclusion of abnormal background signals should begin with inspecting the sample cell, then the laser source and lens, and finally, the alignment system. ## Related Particle Size Analyzer. Static and dynamic arrays differ mainly in how memory is allocated, how size is managed, and how flexible they are at runtime. + Static array: size and memory layout determined at compile time (or fixed on allocation). + Static array: size is fixed and cannot be changed after allocation. Static and dynamic arrays differ mainly in how memory is allocated, how size is managed, and how flexible they are at runtime. + Static array: size and memory layout determined at compile time (or fixed on allocation). + Static array: size is fixed and cannot be changed after allocation. Summary: static arrays are fixed-size with compile-time or fixed allocation and minimal runtime overhead; dynamic arrays allocate on the heap and support resizing at the cost of allocation and management complexity. results.title: Static vs Dynamic Alert Thresholds for Monitoring | eG Innovations
results.content: Enterprise grade products and native cloud monitoring (e.g., Microsoft Azure Monitor used with services such as AVD) will usually include options to use both static and dynamic thresholds and occasionally combine them. For example, within Microsoft Azure Monitor, whilst the actual value of the metric thresholds will be calculated within the product based on past learned behavior the administrator needs to configure each metrics and many associated parameters (see Figure 1), such as alert severity, granularity of sampling (over how long a time period is an anomaly is considered significant) and sensitivity (is a deviation of 20% or 200% from normal considered reportable). * Further details on static and dynamic thresholding strategies is available in a free white paper: White Paper | Make IT Service Monitoring Simple & Proactive with AIOps Powered Intelligent Thresholding & Alerting (eginnovations.com).

They use known population info to adjust estimates, reducing bias from non-response and sampling errors. The choice between post-stratification and calibration depends on the type and quality of available auxiliary data. * Post-stratification adjusts survey estimates using population information known after data collection. * Improves precision of estimates by reducing sampling variability. * Calibration estimators adjust sample weights to match known population totals for auxiliary variables. * GREG incorporates auxiliary information through a regression model of the survey variable. * Choice of method depends on available auxiliary information and survey design complexity. * Calibration constraints ensure sample weights reproduce known population totals for auxiliary variables. + Where $w\_i$ are the calibrated weights, $x\_i$ are auxiliary variable values, and $X$ is the population total.
